interpretation: Both declared off/on diagnostic invocations pass all thirteen original individual gates with stable inputs and complete 200-request serial profiles. Signature-preserving wrappers retain only numeric wall/thread-CPU/queue observations, labels and ordinals; addresses remain in memory only. No intervention, extra RPC, workload, SDK, policy, deadline, threshold or priority change.

Instrumented serial wall p95 is approximately 9.639 ms off and 10.793 ms on; this pair is diagnostic and cannot qualify the original fixed five-pair cohort. Every earlier failed qualification remains failed.

Server native-hook wall p95 is approximately 2.173 ms off / 2.187 ms on, while client hook-header wait is 4.515 / 6.069 ms. Marginal phase quantiles overlap and cannot be added or used alone to attribute the tail.

On-mode request ordinal171 takes22.585ms overall, including17.586ms threadCPU inside the server native wrapper. Other tails include long wall waits with small CPU in directory/route/client-state phases. Off mode also has unrelated route and policy tails. These observations do not support a single pool/queue or native evaluator bottleneck.

Wrappers allocate and retain per-phase observations and can themselves trigger collection or change scheduling. A CPU spike is not proof of production GC, and no global collector/scheduler or product identity check is changed. Next isolate collection/long-hold correlation with a smaller observer before selecting a correction.
